title: X (Twitter) Cards markup
description: The `twitter:*` meta tags that turn a shared link into a card on X. The companion to `ogp:article:1.0`: same `<meta>` channel, and the pair is normally shipped together, which is why a site with Open Graph tags and no card tags is the usual half-done state. Only `twitter:card` is required. `twitter:title`, `twitter:description` and `twitter:image` fall back to their `og:` equivalents, so requiring them here would fail pages that are correct — but `twitter:card` has no fallback, and without it X picks no card type at all. Like Open Graph, this checks something no build tool checks: nothing fails when the tags are wrong, the link just renders badly everywhere it is shared. In HTML these sit on `<meta name="…">`; in front matter they are ordinary quoted keys. See https://developer.x.com/en/docs/x-for-websites/cards/overview/markup

handle.description: An X handle, with or without the leading `@`. Fifteen characters at most, letters, digits and underscores only — the pattern rejects an email address or a profile URL, which is how this field is usually written wrong.

accountId.description: A numeric account id. Typed for both channels: from HTML every attribute is a string, while front matter can carry a real number.

httpsUrl.description: An absolute HTTPS URL. X does not load card media over plain HTTP.

pixels.description: A pixel count. Typed for both channels: the pattern constrains the HTML string form, the minimum the front matter number form.

twitter:card.description: The card type. Required, and the one tag with no `og:` fallback — omit it and no card renders at all. Enumerated because X defines exactly these four and ignores anything else.

twitter:site.description: The handle of the site the card belongs to.

twitter:site:id.description: The numeric id of the site's account, an alternative to `twitter:site`.

twitter:creator.description: The handle of the content's author.

twitter:creator:id.description: The numeric id of the author's account.

twitter:title.description: The card's title. Truncated past 70 characters, so the length is a real limit rather than a style rule. Falls back to `og:title`.

twitter:description.description: The card's description. Truncated past 200 characters. Falls back to `og:description`.

twitter:image.description: The card's image. Must be HTTPS — an HTTP image is dropped and the card renders without it. Falls back to `og:image`.

twitter:image:alt.description: Alternative text for the image, for people using a screen reader. 420 characters at most.

twitter:player.description: The HTTPS URL of the iframe player. Player cards only.

twitter:player:stream.description: The URL of a raw video stream, as an alternative to an iframe player.

twitter:app:country.description: The two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for the app store to use. Uppercase.

then.description: A player card is the one type with its own required set: without the player URL and its dimensions there is nothing to embed, and X falls back to no card rather than to a summary.
